title: SRD coverage: mundane birds, fish and aquatic animals
summary: Independently authored GURPS builds for the 20 bird, fish and aquatic identities issue #38 enumerates. Re-drafted from the rules alone after an earlier draft was written with fitted bands from an outside reference in hand; see decision 7 of review/policy/srd-independent-build-policy.md. Size Modifier is read off the published table keyed to the creature's longest dimension, which is why several records here are smaller than their mass alone would suggest — a pond frog is 13 cm long whatever it weighs. ST is derived from Basic Lift and from what the animal actually shifts: prey carried, a rider borne, a carcass dragged. Perception and Will are reasoned per creature from the sense it hunts or evades by, rather than applied as one figure across the batch, which is why a hawk and a sea horse are eight points apart. Movement carries most of the mechanical weight here, so every spec declares a `movement` block: the published Move is the primary medium's cruising Move, and Enhanced Move is reported as a sprint figure in the notes rather than folded into it. Every spec records `massKg` and states its length in `notes`, so both derivations are checkable.

monsters.name: Bat
monsters.lair: A cave roof, belfry or hollow tree, shared with hundreds more of its kind.

attacks.name: Bite
attacks.notes: Barely a wound; the bat is a nuisance and a disease vector, not a threat.

monsters.description: A hand-sized insect hunter that navigates a pitch-dark cavern by sound alone and never touches a wall doing it. One is harmless. A roost disturbed at dusk is a wall of them coming out at once, which is worth a Fright Check and nothing else.
notes: Longest dimension about 25 cm with the wings out, which is the published table's SM -5 row.
ST is the floor: 30 g of animal carrying nothing but itself.
Perception is only moderately raised. The bat's edge is not general alertness but one extraordinary sense, and Scanning Sense, Ultrahearing and Acute Hearing 4 are where that is paid for.
Ground Move is deliberately crippled: a bat on the floor drags itself.

monsters.name: Blood Hawk
monsters.lair: A stick nest on a cliff ledge, ringed with the bones of whatever the flock last brought down.

attacks.name: Talons
attacks.notes: Struck on the stoop, at the eyes and scalp. Cannot parry.

monsters.description: A red-eyed raptor with none of a hawk's caution, hunting in flocks that mob anything warm-blooded crossing open ground. Individually one is a bird. Five arriving out of the sun, all going for the same face, is how travellers lose an eye.
notes: Body about 60 cm; Size Modifier follows body length, not the wingspan, because the wings fold.
ST from Basic Lift: it can carry roughly its own 1.5 kg for a short flight.
Will is high for a bird of this size and that is the point of the creature — it commits to a target that could kill it.

monsters.name: Crab
monsters.lair: A wet crevice under a rock at the tide line.

attacks.name: Pincer
attacks.notes: A nipped finger. Cannot parry.

monsters.description: Shore vermin in a shell three sizes too good for it, sidling out of the rocks to strip anything the tide leaves. The pincers hurt and the shell is genuinely hard for something this small, which is the whole of its defence and most of its personality.
notes: About 40 cm across with the legs spread, which is the SM -4 row.
DR is full armour, not Tough Skin: a carapace is shell, and a scratch that would slip past thick hide does not slip past this.

monsters.name: Crocodile
monsters.lair: A mud bank above a slow river, with a scraped nest hollow and a slide worn down into the water.

attacks.name: Bite
attacks.notes: Closes and holds; the crocodile does not let go to bite again.

attacks.name: Death Roll
attacks.notes: Against a target it already has in its jaws, the crocodile rolls its whole body. No attack roll; the victim rolls ST or DX to break the grip or is dragged under and drowned.

monsters.description: Four metres of armoured patience lying as a log until the moment it is not. It takes prey at the water's edge, drags it in, and drowns it, and its hide turns a spear that would go through anything else this side of a dragon. Out of the water it is slow. In the water nothing is winning.
notes: Four metres nose to tail puts it on the SM +2 row. Length, not mass, is what the published table reads.
ST from Basic Lift: it drags an 80 kg carcass into the water, which is the job its strength has to do.
DR is full armour rather than Tough Skin: osteoderms are bone plates, not thick hide.

Added after a post-hoc comparison against independent GURPS fan conversions of this creature: Peripheral Vision; Rapid Healing; Resistant To Disease; the Tracking skill, which a creature with Discriminatory Smell should always have. The comparison surfaced the gap; the build is still ours.

monsters.name: Frog
monsters.lair: Reed beds and pond margins; in a dry season, whatever mud is still damp.

attacks.name: Bite
attacks.notes: It eats flies. This entry is included for completeness.

monsters.description: A pond frog, present in any wetland by the hundred and dangerous to nothing larger than a moth. It matters at the table as a familiar, a component, an alchemical ingredient and a sound that stops when something else arrives.
notes: About 13 cm nose to vent with the legs gathered, which is the SM -7 row. An earlier draft had it three steps larger because it was sized from a mass band rather than from the published length table.
Added after a post-hoc comparison against independent GURPS fan conversions of this creature: Peripheral Vision. The comparison surfaced the gap; the build is still ours.

monsters.name: Giant Crab
monsters.lair: A flooded sea cave or sunken wreck, floored with cracked shell and picked bone.

attacks.name: Pincer
attacks.notes: Takes hold and does not open again while the crab lives. Cannot parry.

monsters.description: A crab the size of a war shield, sidling out of the surf on legs that clatter on stone. The shell shrugs off a sword cut and the claws close hard enough to take a hand off at the wrist. It is slow, stupid and almost impossible to hurt from the front.
notes: About two metres across the leg span, which is the SM 0 row.
ST raised from an earlier draft: Basic Lift has to cover dragging a body back to the water, which is the thing the creature is for.
DR is full armour: a carapace is shell, not hide.

monsters.name: Giant Lizard
monsters.lair: A rock cleft or cave mouth warmed by the afternoon sun, littered with shed skin.

attacks.name: Bite
attacks.notes: A filthy wound; bites that do not kill often fester.

attacks.name: Claws
attacks.notes: Cannot parry.

monsters.description: A monitor grown to the length of a horse, tasting the air with a forked tongue and climbing a cave wall as easily as it crosses the floor. Deep folk keep them as mounts and pack beasts; left wild they are unhurried, unfrightened, and entirely willing to eat a person.
notes: Three metres nose to tail, which is the SM +1 row.
ST from Basic Lift: it carries a 40 kg carcass up a rock face.

Added after a post-hoc comparison against independent GURPS fan conversions of this creature: Peripheral Vision; the Tracking skill, which a creature with Discriminatory Smell should always have. The comparison surfaced the gap; the build is still ours.

monsters.name: Giant Sea Horse
monsters.lair: Kelp forest and reef shallows, anchored by the tail to whatever holds still.

attacks.name: Ram
attacks.notes: Driven with the whole body; the armoured snout is the only part of it built to hit anything.

monsters.description: Ridden by sea elves and sahuagin alike, and worth more than a good horse. It is armoured in bony rings, placid to the point of stubbornness, and slower than anything that wants to eat it — which is why it is a mount and not a hunter.
notes: Three metres from crown to curled tail, which is the SM +1 row.
ST is set by what a mount has to do: Basic Lift must carry an armed rider. That raised it from an earlier draft, where it had been scaled from mass and could not have borne one.
Deliberately slow: Basic Move is bought down, because a sea horse's whole body plan trades speed for armour and station-keeping.
Added after a post-hoc comparison against independent GURPS fan conversions of this creature: Peripheral Vision. The comparison surfaced the gap; the build is still ours.

monsters.name: Giant Shark
monsters.lair: None; it holds a stretch of open water and patrols it.

attacks.name: Bite
attacks.notes: Rows of serrated teeth on jaws wide enough to take a rower and his oar together.

monsters.description: Six metres of shark that has stopped treating boats as too large. It arrives from below and behind, takes one bite, and circles while whatever is left of the target bleeds. Skin like coarse rasp, no expression, and no reason at all to stop.
notes: Six metres, which is the SM +3 row.
ST from Basic Lift: it carries off a 250 kg piece of whatever it bit.

Added after a post-hoc comparison against independent GURPS fan conversions of this creature: the Tracking skill, which a creature with Discriminatory Smell should always have. The comparison surfaced the gap; the build is still ours.

monsters.name: Giant Toad
monsters.lair: A wallow under a rotting log at the edge of standing water.

attacks.name: Bite
attacks.notes: The toad swallows what it can and works on the rest.

attacks.name: Tongue
attacks.notes: Lashes out a hex, sticks, and drags a lighter target into reach of the mouth.

attacks.name: Toxic Skin
attacks.notes: Anything that bites or grapples the toad bare-handed rolls HT or is nauseated and blurred of vision for minutes. No attack roll; contact alone does it.

monsters.description: A toad the size of a hound, sitting so still in the reeds that it reads as a stone until the tongue comes out. It eats anything it can get into its mouth, which at this size includes a halfling, and its skin sweats a poison that punishes anyone who grabs it.
notes: About 1.5 m gathered, which is the SM 0 row. An earlier draft had it a step larger, sized from mass rather than from the published length table.
ST from Basic Lift: it swallows something the weight of a halfling.
DR 0 is deliberate. An amphibian's skin is thin, wet and permeable — which is also what makes the toxin work. The toughness is in HT and HP, not hide.
Added after a post-hoc comparison against independent GURPS fan conversions of this creature: Peripheral Vision. The comparison surfaced the gap; the build is still ours.

monsters.name: Giant Vulture
monsters.lair: A fouled ledge above a caravan road, in sight of everywhere anything ever dies.

attacks.name: Beak
attacks.notes: A hooked beak built for opening a carcass.

attacks.name: Talons
attacks.notes: Cannot parry.

monsters.description: A carrion bird with a three-metre span and enough intelligence to work out that a struggling party will be dead soon. They circle for a day, drop to the ground as a group, and start on whoever stopped moving first — and they are not always careful about confirming it.
notes: Body about 1.5 m, which is the SM 0 row; the three-metre span is wingspan and the wings fold. An earlier draft sized it from the span.
IQ 5 is deliberate. The SRD presents these as calculating rather than merely hungry, and Will and Per follow from it.

Added after a post-hoc comparison against independent GURPS fan conversions of this creature: the Tracking skill, which a creature with Discriminatory Smell should always have. The comparison surfaced the gap; the build is still ours.

monsters.name: Hawk
monsters.lair: A high nest on a crag or an old tree, reused for years.

attacks.name: Talons
attacks.notes: Delivered at the end of a stoop. Cannot parry.

monsters.description: Eyes that resolve a mouse from the top of a tower, and a dive that arrives before the sound does. As an encounter a hawk is scenery. As a trained bird it is a scout, a messenger and the reason a hunting party eats, and a falconer's hawk is worth more than his horse.
notes: Body about 50 cm, which is the SM -4 row.
Perception is the highest in this batch, and deliberately so: eyesight is the one thing a hawk is unarguably exceptional at, and Acute Vision and Telescopic Vision sit on top of it.

monsters.name: Hunter Shark
monsters.lair: None; it works a coastline and follows whatever bleeds.

attacks.name: Bite
attacks.notes: One pass, one bite, and away before anything can answer it.

monsters.description: The shark that has decided a swimmer is food rather than a question. Three and a half metres of it, tracking blood across half a mile of water and closing from whichever side has no eyes on it. Not malicious — simply extremely good at one thing.
notes: Three and a half metres, which is the SM +2 row.
ST from Basic Lift: it takes a 120 kg piece away with it.

Added after a post-hoc comparison against independent GURPS fan conversions of this creature: the Tracking skill, which a creature with Discriminatory Smell should always have. The comparison surfaced the gap; the build is still ours.

monsters.name: Owl
monsters.lair: A hollow in an old tree, or the rafters of a barn nobody uses after dark.

attacks.name: Talons
attacks.notes: Cannot parry.

monsters.description: It hunts by hearing in total darkness and flies without making any sound at all — a wing edge combed into silence, so the mouse never learns anything is coming. Wizards keep them for the same reason poachers fear them: an owl sees a night camp perfectly and is never noticed watching it.
notes: Body about 50 cm, which is the SM -4 row.
Perception is as high as the hawk's but paid for differently: an owl's exceptional sense is hearing, and Acute Hearing 5 and Night Vision 9 are where that lands.

monsters.name: Porpoise
monsters.lair: None; the pod follows the fish.

attacks.name: Ram
attacks.notes: A pod will ram a shark to death in company; one on its own will not try.

monsters.description: Bright, sociable and genuinely curious about boats, travelling in pods that will escort a hull for miles. Sailors count them lucky and are not entirely wrong: a pod harrying a shark has saved swimmers, and their squealing carries far enough underwater to be a warning if anyone can read it.
notes: About 1.8 m, which is the SM 0 row.
IQ 6 is deliberate and the highest in this batch: a porpoise is genuinely clever, and Will follows from it.
DR 1 is blubber rather than hide, which is why it is Tough Skin.

monsters.name: Quipper
monsters.lair: Warm slow water, and any pool that something has died in recently.

attacks.name: Bite
attacks.notes: One bite is a scratch. The point of a quipper is that there are never one of them.

monsters.description: A hand-length carnivorous fish with a bad temper and worse company. Alone it can barely break skin. In the numbers it actually appears in, a quipper shoal strips a fallen pack animal to bone in the time it takes to wade to the bank.
notes: About 25 cm, which is the SM -5 row.
Rated as a single fish. The shoal is the threat and belongs in the swarm batch, not here.

monsters.name: Reef Shark
monsters.lair: A reef channel it shares with several more of its kind.
monsters.description: Small as sharks go and rarely interested in anything person-sized, until several of them are and the water is already cloudy. Reef sharks hunt in loose company over coral, and what makes them dangerous is arithmetic rather than size.
notes: About two metres, which is the SM 0 row.
ST from Basic Lift: 25 kg carried off, which is a bite's worth and no more.

Added after a post-hoc comparison against independent GURPS fan conversions of this creature: the Tracking skill, which a creature with Discriminatory Smell should always have. The comparison surfaced the gap; the build is still ours.

monsters.name: Sea Horse
monsters.lair: Eelgrass and coral, held by a curled tail against the current.

attacks.name: Snap
attacks.notes: It eats things smaller than a fingernail. This entry exists so the record rates as something rather than nothing.

monsters.description: A thumb-length fish that swims upright, holds station by its tail, and is armoured in bony rings against absolutely nothing that matters. It is a component, a curiosity and a familiar, and it is the reason anyone believes the giant version could be ridden.
notes: About 15 cm upright, which is the SM -7 row. An earlier draft had it two steps larger, sized from a mass band rather than from the published length table.
Added after a post-hoc comparison against independent GURPS fan conversions of this creature: Peripheral Vision. The comparison surfaced the gap; the build is still ours.

monsters.name: Shark
monsters.lair: None; open water and whatever a ship throws over the side.

attacks.name: Bite
attacks.notes: Smells blood at a distance no one can verify and arrives sooner than expected.

monsters.description: The ordinary shark of open water: two and a half metres, endlessly moving, and drawn to a wreck from further off than anyone in the water would like. It tests before it commits, which is the only reason survivors exist to describe it.
notes: Two and a half metres, which is the SM +1 row.
ST from Basic Lift: 50 kg taken away.

Added after a post-hoc comparison against independent GURPS fan conversions of this creature: the Tracking skill, which a creature with Discriminatory Smell should always have. The comparison surfaced the gap; the build is still ours.

monsters.name: Vulture
monsters.lair: A ledge or dead tree with a long view over open country.

attacks.name: Beak
attacks.notes: It will not start a fight. It will finish a meal.

monsters.description: No threat and a great deal of information. Vultures circling mean something died in that direction within the day, and a GM who describes them has told the party where to go without saying a word. On the ground they are ugly, unhurried and appalling to be downwind of.
notes: Body about 80 cm, which is the SM -2 row.
IQ 5 for the same reason as the giant vulture: these are patient, calculating birds rather than merely hungry ones.

Added after a post-hoc comparison against independent GURPS fan conversions of this creature: the Tracking skill, which a creature with Discriminatory Smell should always have. The comparison surfaced the gap; the build is still ours.
